page: Microsoft Azure E96ias_v4 is an isolated, memory-optimized virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 7452 processor on the x86_64 architecture, operating at 3.35 GHz across 48 physical cores and 96 dedicated vCPUs with hyper-threading enabled. Memory capacity totals 672.0 GB of RAM, providing 7.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance includes 1443 GB of local SSD storage and does not feature GPU acceleration.

Benchmark evaluations reveal balanced multi-core throughput alongside strong cryptographic and caching execution. In PassMark testing, the instance achieves top-tier results in CPU encryption alongside strong scores in overall CPU rating, extended instructions, and memory subsystem performance. Cache-level memory throughput is high, reaching 3921.34 GB/s on small-block read workloads, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reaches 415.45 GB/s. However, per-core computation shows limitations; stress-ng single-core performance places in the bottom 10 percent, and large-model prompt processing reflects the expected constraints of CPU-only execution on 70B parameter models.

With 672.0 GB of RAM, 1443 GB of local SSD capacity, and dedicated isolated host assignment, the E96ias_v4 is designed for memory-intensive infrastructure. High-concurrency operations are validated by Redis benchmarking delivering 72.45 million SET operations per second, alongside strong Clang software compilation scores. Workloads requiring extreme single-threaded clock speed or dedicated machine learning acceleration should consider alternative instances.
description: Microsoft Azure E96ias_v4 is an isolated, memory-optimized instance powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 7452 processor running at 3.35 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it provides 48 physical cores, 96 vCPUs, and 672.0 GB of system memory, alongside 1443 GB of bundled local SSD storage without GPU hardware. Benchmark results demonstrate strong cryptographic performance with top-tier PassMark encryption metrics, strong multi-threaded compilation throughput, and high cached memory throughput reaching 3921.34 GB/s. High-concurrency in-memory data processing is confirmed by Redis benchmarking yielding 72.45 million SET operations per second. However, single-threaded execution scores such as stress-ng occupy lower percentiles, indicating that throughput scales primarily via core concurrency and memory volume. The server profile fits enterprise-grade in-memory caches, distributed databases, and high-concurrency parallel software build environments.
